name: Cartograph Atlas — Server-Authoritative Stable-Handle Map with Bounded Tiled Rendering
overview:
ONE unified architecture synthesizing the four candidate designs (which are ~85% the same design independently rediscovered) into a single coherent end-state. It rests on a SHARED SPINE that all four agree on and that the Stage-1 report names as THE highest-leverage fix, plus a render layer sequenced to de-risk.

DECISIVE CONTEXT CORRECTION (verified on disk): the engine is UE 5.6.1-CSS (FactoryGame.uproject EngineAssociation="5.6.1-CSS"), NOT 5.3.2 as the prompt assumed. This REMOVES nearly every "needs-newer-UE" gate: native SceneCapture orthographic tiling, current AbstractInstance per-instance custom data, UE::Tasks, and GPU Scene auto-instancing are all available. Every technique below is re-tagged against 5.6.1.

The three highest-leverage primitives already ship in this repo's Plugins/ and are verified present: AbstractInstance (stable FInstanceOwnerHandlePtr handles, O(1) SetInstanceFromDataStatic/RemoveInstance with internal swap-patch, SetCustomPrimitiveDataOnHandle, NumCustomDataFloats, MarkDirtyDeferred; currently commented out in Cartograph.Build.cs), ReliableMessaging (SendTaggedMessage over a chunked/acked/windowed transport, SizeType=int32 so the int16 overflow is gone by construction, TCP transport links on dedicated server), and UE5Coro (vendored, FTickTimeBudget). The redesign is therefore largely an INTEGRATION project, not a from-scratch research bet.

THE SHARED SPINE (adopt verbatim, kills root causes 1+2+leak+O(N^2) load at once): (1) Identity = a stable generational handle, NEVER a positional index. (2) Storage = an SoA/ECS column store keyed by that handle, with engine-as-truth on the host (no second copy). (3) Spatial index = a uniform fixed-cell hash grid over the constexpr world bounds keyed by the handle. (4) Z-filter = a SEPARATE coarse Z-band index decoupled from storage, deleting the operator<=> Z-sort coupling. (5) Async = one never-cancelled convergent compositor draining a monotonic dirty set under a frame-relative budget, with UE::Tasks workers for POD packing. (6) Network = delete the slice RCO, use ReliableMessaging with delta-by-tile-version per-AoI pull. (7) Partition = host/listen reads engine subsystems as truth (zero second copy); dedicated server holds indices + slim blobs and renders nothing; dedicated clients hold a slim AoI store only.

RENDER (the one real divergence, sequenced not chosen): Phase A ships the spine on the existing FCanvas with bounded per-tile EndDraw + scissored hardware clear + persistent target (Epic-officially-sanctioned TDR fix, zero custom shaders) — this alone designs out crash #14. Phase B promotes the render PRIMITIVE to a custom Slate SLeafWidget emitting FSlateDrawElement::MakeCustomVerts with a per-instance buffer (~10x cheaper than FCanvas-to-RT per Froyok, deletes the persistent VRAM target and the process-wide FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook). Phase C (gated end-state) the GPU-instanced AbstractInstance marker layer + orthographic USceneCaptureComponent2D with native bEnableOrthographicTiling, adopted ONLY after validating GetViewOwner/ShowOnlyActors capture isolation on the CSS fork. The hand-rolled RDG/custom-shader rasterizer (architecture #1's primary path) is REJECTED as primary and demoted to a profiled optional Phase N.

NET at 1M buildings: host dataset RAM ~360-430 MB -> ~10-40 MB of indices (geometry read live from the engine); dedicated-client RAM ~360-430 MB -> ~26 MB slim AoI store; VRAM 256 MB monolith -> fixed ~64-96 MB atlas (Phase A) -> ~0 persistent (Phase B); per-event CPU O(N)-rising-with-session -> flat O(1); initial load O(N^2) -> O(N); join from a crash (#9) to a backpressured O(AoI) stream; TDR crash (#14) structurally impossible.
dataModel:
SHARED SPINE — adopted verbatim across all four candidates; this IS the verified Stage-1 end-state.

IDENTITY: a stable generational handle FBuildingHandle{uint32 slot, uint16 gen}, NEVER a positional index into a Z-sorted array. This single decision deletes the entire (Z-sorted TArray + TQuadTree<int32> + BuildingDataIndexRedirector) triad and with it root cause 1: the O(N) reindex per add/remove, the O(N^2) initial load (the redirector reindex branch is provably never taken during the monotonic load — confirmed in problemDigest), and the never-compacting tombstone leak (per-event scan length was = cumulative-lifetime-adds; now it is irrelevant because there is no redirector). The generation counter makes handles ABA-safe so network deltas and UI picks never alias a recycled TSparseArray/AbstractInstance slot.

STORAGE = SoA/ECS COLUMN STORE (architecture #1's data model, the furthest-going and most cache-friendly), keyed by the handle, backed by TSparseArray slots (O(1) Add/RemoveAt, free-list reuse, positions never shift). Columns: Pos (FVector3f, 12B — single-precision is sufficient, ~0.05 cm worst-case error at the 7.5 km edge, and NetSerialize already drops scale+quat proving the minimal record), Yaw (packed int16/float16, 2B — top-down needs only yaw, no quat, no scale), ClassId (uint16 index into the per-class table, 2B), Type (uint8 Icon/Rectangle/Spline/Wire/Beam), ExtraIndex (uint32 into typed side-tables for splines/wires/beams so a belt never pays for a rectangle cache). NOTHING that is a pure function of transform+class is stored: ScreenPosition, Corners[4], Size, Rotation, VisualBoxCache, FNormalDataCache/FRectangleDataCache are ALL DELETED (~152-192 B/building of recomputable draw cache) and recomputed at draw via one shared pure ComputeDrawGeometry(record, classInfo) helper (must reproduce the old FillInCache math pixel-identically — extract once, diff-render a large save, then delete the stored fields).

PER-CLASS TABLE: TMap<uint16 classId, FClassDrawInfo> ClassDrawTable, sized by distinct CLASSES (hundreds), built once at gather: icon texture, footprint size, category color, layer, extra-rotation. The four per-building pointers the old design stored (CategoryData/LayerData/SplineData/WireData) collapse to one hash lookup per class at draw.

SPATIAL INDEX = uniform fixed-cell hash grid over the constexpr bounds (WEST/EAST/NORTH/SOUTH verified present in CartographGameInstanceModule.h). Because bounds are fixed and ~750000x750000 cm, use a flat TArray of cells (e.g. ~256 m cells aligned to the tile grid) each a small TArray<FBuildingHandle>. Insert = O(cells-covered) push by stable handle; remove = O(1) swap-remove by handle (no equal-Z linear == scan, no redirector walk); query = O(cells-in-rect + hits). Replaces TQuadTree<int32>'s 40 B/element FBox2D entirely; multi-cell buildings (long belts, large foundations) store a small per-record cell list consistently on move/remove.

Z-FILTER = SEPARATE coarse Z-band index (~64 fixed 1 m bands, TArray<TArray<FBuildingHandle>> or per-cell band bitmask), decoupled from storage so the master columns never need sorting. The height slider selects a band range, intersected with the spatial query. This deletes the operator<=> Z-sort coupling that was the single decision forcing unstable positions, and turns OnZFilterUpdated from an O(N) full re-walk into a band-range select. (In Phase C with AbstractInstance, worldZ rides as per-instance custom data and the filter becomes a material clip() — see renderPipeline.)

STORED vs RECOMPUTED vs QUERIED-FROM-ENGINE:
- HOST (listen/single-player): stored = grid + Z-band index + ClassDrawTable + (Phase C) AbstractInstance handles. QUERIED live from the engine per dirty cell, by const-ref (NOT by value): AFGBuildableSubsystem::GetAllBuildablesRef() + AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem::mBuildableClassToInstanceArray. No FBuildingData store at all. RECOMPUTED at draw: all screen geometry. (The current "Intentional copies" by-value gather at module.cpp:455 is deleted — pass by const-ref, removing the O(N) deep copy that transiently doubles the factory at load.)
- DEDICATED-SERVER CLIENT: holds the slim SoA columns (~24-28 B/building) for its AoI tiles only, fed by the network — its sole source since it lacks the subsystems. RECOMPUTES geometry locally.
- DEDICATED SERVER: holds grid + Z-index + per-tile slim blobs; renders nothing.

REPO-VERIFIED REFINEMENT (Phase C only): do NOT hand-build a TSparseArray instance buffer + manual StructuredBuffer patching (architecture #1 over-engineers this). Back the render store with AbstractInstance (Plugins/AbstractInstance): FInstanceOwnerHandlePtr is the stable handle, SetInstanceFromDataStatic/RemoveInstance are O(1) with internal swap-patch, SetCustomPrimitiveDataOnHandle carries worldZ/layerId/colorIndex via NumCustomDataFloats. CAVEATS verified on disk: the handle is TSharedPtr<...,ESPMode::NotThreadSafe> = game-thread-only (so AbstractInstance mutation never moves to a worker), and the manager builds ULightweightCollisionComponent by default (disable collision for a visual-only marker layer). The CPU-side spatial/Z indices above remain regardless of render path (needed for picking, dirty-rect bookkeeping, and the slim-blob network packing on dedicated servers).
renderPipeline:
The render layer is the ONE real divergence among the four candidates. Resolution: keep the tile/dirty-rect CONCEPT for CPU-side culling + budgeted convergence + per-tile network versioning, but SEQUENCE the IMAGE backend to de-risk. Do NOT pick one variant outright; ship A, promote to B, gate C.

PHASE A (PRIMARY, ships first — Epic-officially-sanctioned TDR fix, zero custom shaders): bounded per-tile FCanvas EndDraw + scissored hardware clear on a persistent target. The fixed world is partitioned into a tile grid (e.g. 256 m tiles aligned to World Partition cell granularity). The render target is a persistent UCanvasRenderTarget2D, NEVER fully cleared (UpdateResourceImmediate with the clear-on-receive flag false — verify the 5.6.1-CSS signature) and bAutoGenerateMips DISABLED (else EndDraw kicks a whole-texture mip pass that silently defeats the scissor). Build events mark touched tiles dirty in a TBitArray. Per frame a budgeted scheduler pops up to K dirty tiles; for each it issues a true scissored RHIClearRenderTargetView bounded to that tile's rect (a near-free hardware clear of ~1 MB vs the current full-screen 67 M-texel / 256 MB opaque FCanvasTileItem) via an RDG/RHI AddPass, then redraws only the buildings the grid reports in that tile (Z-band filtered), then EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget. EACH TILE IS A SEPARATE GPU COMMAND BUFFER SUBMISSION — this is exactly Epic's documented TDR-avoidance pattern (UE GPU-crash doc: "each tile is submitted as a separate command buffer"). A megabase first-paint drains across ceil(dirtyTiles/K) frames; no single submission approaches the ~2 s Windows TDR, so crash #14 is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE. Drop RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE from 8192 to ~4096 (match the uasset SizeX/Y) — 256 MB -> 64 MB VRAM, the constexpr ORIGIN_UV/PIXEL_PER_CENTIMETER stay self-consistent.

PHASE B (PREFERRED 2D DEFAULT — the single best render idea in the dossiers): replace the FCanvas-to-RT path with a custom Slate SLeafWidget whose OnPaint emits FSlateDrawElement::MakeCustomVerts with a per-instance buffer — one instanced draw batching ALL buildings (a unit quad/line per building). Per Froyok this is ~10x cheaper on the render thread than FCanvas-to-RT (~1.3 ms vs ~12 ms for the same work) AND deletes the persistent VRAM render target entirely (64 MB -> ~0 persistent; the on-screen panel composites via Slate's own swap-chain pass) AND removes the process-wide FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook by construction (the cross-mod static_cast hazard + per-batch tax flagged in Stage-1). Z-ORDER: MakeCustomVerts is not depth-sorted across instances, so bake draw order into instance order via the Z-band index (paint back-to-front — exactly the ordering the Z-band index already produces). ZOOM-LOD: re-expressed as instance-count culling per zoom (cull instances to the visible viewport clip rect), replacing texture mips. The tile/dirty-rect machinery is retained for CPU-side culling + network versioning, not as an image store. NOTE: UE 5.5+ async-Slate/parallel-RHI (~2x) IS available on 5.6.1 and amplifies this — but tune the frame budget conservatively and validate.

PHASE C (GATED END-STATE — adopt ONLY after validating capture isolation on the CSS fork): GPU-instanced AbstractInstance marker layer (one ULightweightHISM per class on a hidden marker actor, collision disabled) captured top-down by an orthographic USceneCaptureComponent2D with NATIVE bEnableOrthographicTiling + NumXTiles/NumYTiles (available on 5.6, splits one ortho capture across frames = a second engine-native TDR bound; requires CaptureSource=SceneColor, bCaptureEveryFrame=false + debounced dirty flag). Per-instance custom data (worldZ, layerId, colorIndex) drives a material clip() for Z-band + layer filtering with ZERO per-event CPU. Add/remove become O(1) handle ops. ISOLATION risk: PrimitiveRenderMode=UseShowOnlyList + ShowOnlyActors(MarkerActor) + GetViewOwner() override — UNVERIFIED on the CSS renderer fork (the Cartograph_2.0 POC used exactly this but never compiled). CAUTION per Tessera's evidence: UE5 ISM AddInstance/RemoveInstance regressed for high-churn megabases (Chaos collision rebuild) — MITIGATE by disabling collision (AbstractInstance builds it by default, verified) + batching via MarkDirtyDeferred. NEVER make Phase C the only renderer; the bounded Slate/canvas path stays the always-available fallback.

REJECTED as primary: architecture #1's hand-rolled RDG compute/indirect-draw rasterizer with custom global shaders — highest feasibility risk on the CSS fork (the Cartograph GameFeature is LoadingPhase=Default with no Shaders dir; needs a PostConfigInit shader module or the ShaderDirectoryMapper trick, and renderer-private headers limit a clean mod). Keep it ONLY as a profiled optional Phase N if a megabase still hitches after C.
asyncThreading:
CONVERGENCE = MONOTONIC ACCUMULATION, never cancel/restart (resolves amplifier root cause 4, identical across all four candidates; articulated most cleanly by #1 and #4).

DELETE the cancel-on-every-event pattern. Today every build hook calls RedrawMap(false) -> Cancel() the in-flight coroutine -> restart -> re-pay the non-cancellable O(N) ingestion under FCancellationGuard, so a belt-drag is a permanent cancel->restart loop producing ZERO completed frames until the player stops. Replace with:

(1) BUILD HOOKS do O(1) work only: patch one column slot / one AbstractInstance handle, insert/erase the handle in the grid + Z-band index, OR the touched tile ids into a monotonic dirty set (TBitArray DirtyTiles + dirty-rect). They enqueue nothing heavy and NEVER touch the compositor. Because ingestion is now O(1) there is no FCancellationGuard-protected O(N) block to re-pay.

(2) A SINGLE long-lived convergent compositor coroutine runs every frame under a FRAME-RELATIVE budget (keep the vendored UE5Coro FTickTimeBudget model — a fraction of frame time, e.g. r.Cartograph.FrameBudgetFraction=0.15, NOT an absolute ms; this is the correct answer to issue #10). It is NEVER cancelled. It drains the dirty set: pops up to K dirty tiles, renders them, and only ever SHRINKS the dirty set — completed tiles stay valid, a tile re-dirtied mid-pass is simply re-queued (coalesced by its bit, so a tile dirtied 100x renders once). Critically, await ONCE PER TILE (or per K buildings), NOT per primitive — this kills the ~9*N per-primitive awaiter + FPlatformTime::Cycles() reads that Stage-1 flagged (today it awaits after every rectangle edge and every spline segment). DirtyCells/dirty-rect accumulation must survive cancellation correctly (the partial_redraw branch lost the dirty rect across cancel/restart — a known regression to design around; here there is no cancel, so it is moot).

(3) OFF THE GAME THREAD via UE::Tasks::Launch (native on 5.6): per-dirty-cell POD snapshot packing and per-tile network-blob serialization/compression on workers. Only pure data transforms (packing FVector3f+yaw+classId into a byte blob) go on workers. STRICTLY game-thread-only and never moved to a worker: reading the live engine buildable arrays (races concurrent builds — snapshot the inputs on the game thread, hand the immutable POD copy to the worker), AbstractInstance handle mutation (FInstanceOwnerHandlePtr is NotThreadSafe — verified on disk), all render-target/Slate-vertex/RHI ops. Keep UE5Coro for the latent frame-budgeted draw drain; use UE::Tasks only for the pure-CPU packing/serialization.

(4) BACKPRESSURE: prioritize tiles in the player's current map-viewport AoI first so the visible map converges first while off-screen tiles lazily catch up; coalesce mass-paste bursts into one render per tile. The explicit user-triggered full-redraw button (#10) just sets all populated tiles dirty.

(5) DEDICATED SERVER: skip ALL draw-oriented bookkeeping (no compositor, no tiles-to-pixels). It only maintains the grid + Z-index + per-tile slim blobs and bumps per-tile versions on the game thread, with snapshot serialization on UE::Tasks workers.

Pre-resolve and PIN all distinct icon textures before any draw/capture pass so the loop never co_awaits AsyncLoadObject mid-pass (a current bug at module.cpp:758 that stalls the open canvas).
networkTransport:
DELETE the hand-rolled slice RCO (CartographRemoteCallObject) wholesale — it is where crash #9 lives: three unchecked *TMap::Find() null-derefs racing the 10 s per-slice timeout, the int16 slice-count overflow at ~63 MB, the move-unsafe FBufferWriter-in-a-TMap, the fixed-2047-byte stack-tail leak, and the per-join synchronous Archive<<CurrentBuildingData on the game thread. None of it survives.

TRANSPORT = the in-repo ReliableMessaging plugin (Plugins/ReliableMessaging), REPO-VERIFIED: UReliableMessagingPlayerComponent::SendTaggedMessage(FGameplayTag, TArray<uint8>) over a chunked/acked/windowed/backpressured transport; SizeType = TArray<uint8>::SizeType (int32) and MessageIdType = uint64, so the int16 slice-overflow bug CLASS is gone BY CONSTRUCTION; per-PlayerController component with disconnect teardown kills the timeout-race null-deref and per-join leak by construction. Transports include TCP (the ReliableMessagingTCP module links on the dedicated-server target where EOS/Steam P2P are denied — so the dedicated-server join path #9 is covered).

DESIGN = DELTA-BY-TILE-VERSION / per-AoI lazy pull, NOT reliable-multicast-per-event (which today fires ClientUpdateBuildingData NetMulticast Reliable per build event and floods the channel):
- VERSIONING: the server bumps a per-tile content version = HASH of the authoritative tile content (NOT a session counter — so reconnect/late join is deterministic and idempotent). A build/remove bumps only the version of the affected tile(s).
- JOIN (fixes #9 by design): the joining client sends its initial map-viewport AoI; the server replies with a small MANIFEST (tile list + version per tile) then streams the per-tile slim blobs for that AoI. No global serialize, no per-joiner full copy: the server holds ONE shared immutable ref-counted snapshot per tile (TSharedRef<const TArray<uint8>>) pinned across all joiners, so join memory is O(joiners + AoI), NOT O(joiners*N). The client renders tiles progressively as they arrive.
- LIVE DELTAS: the server coalesces per-tile version bumps per net-tick and pushes, per client, only the deltas for tiles in that client's AoI; far-away edits invalidate only their tile and never touch the client's current view. A reconnecting/late client pulls only tiles whose version it lacks.

VERIFIED CAVEATS (confirmed in ReliableMessagingPlayerComponent.h) that SHAPE the design:
- SendTaggedMessage takes the payload BY VALUE — so each tile blob is materialized in RAM at send; this REINFORCES the per-tile (slim, ~28 B/record + RLE for empty tiles) design and forbids one whole-dataset blob. Size the in-flight window accordingly.
- The send queue is strict FIFO, not priority-sorted — AoI-visible tiles cannot preempt already-queued far tiles without APP-LEVEL AoI ordering (order the manifest by distance from the viewport center before enqueueing).
- Use a SMALL FIXED gameplay-tag set (manifest / tile / version), NOT a tag-per-tile (tag registration costs a round-trip).
- Initialize the transport + complete the connection handshake at world load (queue tiles until the per-player component reports Connected); keep sends flowing so an idle connection does not hit the default timeout.

WP ALIGNMENT: tiles align 1:1 with World Partition cell granularity so a client entering a new region is an O(1) version check + optional blob fetch, never a recompute. But the map-UI viewport AoI is NOT the world-streaming AoI — the UI viewport rect drives tile pulls; do not conflate them. World Partition is not moddable, so the design only READS source positions to prioritize, never drives cell loading.

EXPLICITLY RULED OUT: UE5 Iris replication — enabling it is a project/Target.cs-level toggle that changes the whole game's replication path, not something a GameFeature mod can flip on CSS's shipped build; and the join problem is a one-shot bulk transfer, not high-frequency many-actor replication. ReliableMessaging is the right tool.
serverClientPartitioning:
EXPLICIT split (architecture #3's server-authoritative thin-client model, reinforced by #1's host-engine-as-truth), designed so the client NEVER recomputes datasets on join or on chunk-load — directly matching the Stage-1 directive.

WHAT IS COMPUTED-ONCE-AND-STORED ON THE SERVER (authoritative; clients never recompute): the uniform grid + Z-band index, the ClassDrawTable, the per-tile content-hash versions, and the per-tile slim instance blobs. These are DERIVED from the engine subsystems, rebuilt cheaply at world-load by one O(N) streaming bucketing pass over AFGBuildableSubsystem / AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem (no O(N^2), no second copy), then kept incrementally correct by the O(1) build hooks. They are a RUNTIME CACHE, deterministically reconstructable from authoritative engine state — see memoryModel/persistence for why they are NOT a save correctness dependency.

HOST = LISTEN-SERVER / SINGLE-PLAYER (server+client in one process): the host reads AFGBuildableSubsystem / AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem as the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH and keeps ZERO second copy — only the grid + Z-index + ClassDrawTable + (Phase C) the render-side AbstractInstance handles. It renders directly from engine transforms; there is NO slim client store and NO network path at all (zero serialization, zero duplication). The map UI reads the host's own indices/render output directly. Same code with the transport stubbed.

DEDICATED SERVER: holds the authoritative indices + per-tile slim blobs + versions but RENDERS NOTHING — no atlas, no Slate widget, no SceneCapture, no FCanvas (saves all VRAM and render-thread cost). Skips all draw-oriented bookkeeping. It is the only place the authoritative derived state lives for thin clients.

DEDICATED-SERVER CLIENT (the only config that holds a per-client record copy): lacks the subsystem data, so it keeps ONLY the slim SoA store (~24-28 B/building) for its AoI tiles, fed by the ReliableMessaging tile stream, and does all rendering locally from those. On map-pan/AoI-change it pulls newly-entered tiles and evicts left tiles (LRU); on a build event it gets a version ping and lazily re-pulls; on a WP chunk-load it does an O(1) version check, never a recompute.

ALIGNMENT TO WORLD PARTITION: tiles map 1:1 onto fixed WP cells so chunk-load is an O(1) version check. DESIGN-AROUND CONSTRAINTS (verified concerns): WP is not moddable (cannot drive server-side region streaming, only read what is loaded); lightweight indices can be RENUMBERED by the engine on its own removals; not all regions are resident on the client. Therefore use GENERATION-GUARDED {class, index} keys and RECONCILE-ON-LOAD; tolerate streamed-out regions; and do NOT conflate the map-UI viewport AoI with the player's world-streaming AoI.

EXPLICIT RESOURCE TRADE: the server spends modest CPU (incremental per-tile content-hash versioning) + RAM (per-tile slim blobs, ~26-28 MB @1M) + bandwidth (only changed AoI tiles + tiny version pings) so that EVERY client avoids recomputing a second full dataset, joins are bounded and crash-free (O(AoI) not O(N)), and chunk-loads are O(1). Cost moves from the many (clients, repeatedly) to the one (server, once per version).
memoryModel:
Peak RAM and VRAM are both DECOUPLED from runaway growth and FLAT across a build/dismantle session — the explicit #14 success criterion (#14's "worsens over ~1 h" signature came from the never-compacting redirector growing the per-event scan with cumulative-lifetime-adds; deleting it removes the signature). Accounting follows architecture #1 (most rigorous), tied with #4 for the host/client split.

WHAT IS DELETED: (a) the ~344-432 B/building FBuildingData second copy and its ~152-192 B precomputed draw caches (FNormalDataCache/FRectangleDataCache/VisualBoxCache, recomputed at draw from the per-class table); (b) the never-compacting BuildingDataIndexRedirector (the session-long O(cumulative-adds) leak); (c) the TQuadTree<int32>'s 40 B/element FBox2D (replaced by the grid); (d) the in-RAM FTransform Scale3D + FQuat (top-down needs only yaw); (e) the by-value engine-map deep copy at load ("Intentional copies", module.cpp:455 — pass by const-ref, removes the O(N) transient doubling).

HOST (listen / single-player): NO geometry copy. Resident = uniform grid (slot ids only, ~4 B/live building amortized) + Z-band index (~4 B/building) + ClassDrawTable (hundreds of entries, KBs) + (Phase C) AbstractInstance instance buffer (~16-64 B/building, render-side, much of it VRAM). Host CPU-RAM for the dataset is ~8-12 B/building of indices vs the ~360-430 MB-equivalent today — geometry is read live from the engine and consumed transiently per dirty cell, never stored.

DEDICATED-SERVER CLIENT: slim SoA columns only for AoI tiles (~24-28 B/building in-AoI, near-zero for streamed-out tiles) + its own render VRAM. 1M buildings in view is never resident — only the AoI working set (a few thousand buildings in a viewport ~ tens of KB to a few MB).

DEDICATED SERVER: per-tile slim blobs (~26-28 MB @1M) + grid + Z-index; NO atlas/VRAM. Shared TSharedRef snapshots pinned across joiners keep join memory O(N), not O(joiners*N).

VRAM: a FIXED CEILING independent of building count — 200k, 1M, or 50M all cost the same because the image is viewport-sized, not factory-sized. Phase A: persistent tile atlas ~64-96 MB (down from the 256 MB monolith; scissored HW clears, no full-screen 256 MB opaque clear). Phase B: persistent target drops toward ~0 (Slate composites via its own swap-chain pass; the MakeCustomVerts instance buffer ~16 B/building is the only count-scaling GPU buffer and can be paged per-AoI). Generational handles add ~4 B/slot. The redirector leak, quadtree append-only growth, and the per-disconnect RCO buffer/timer leak are all gone (ReliableMessaging owns transfer buffers with disconnect teardown).

PERSISTENCE (resolving the cross-candidate conflict toward recomputable-cache): derived state (tiles/versions/grid) is a RECOMPUTABLE RUNTIME CACHE, version = content hash, reconciled in PostLoadGame against the live subsystem arrays. Optionally persist via IFGSaveInterface (ShouldSave -> true) ONLY the grid + slim records to skip the O(N) cold re-bucket on load — content-hash-validated, version-prefixed, with a clean fallback to rebuild from engine arrays when stale. Do NOT embed tile pixel snapshots in the save (architectures #2/#3 default to this; it bloats the save and churns format for data that is cheaply recomputable). Treat the save as a cache, never a correctness dependency.
dataFlow:
END-TO-END, covering build-event, join, and chunk-load flows.

(1) BUILD EVENT (O(1), the hot path): a buildable add/remove fires an SML hook. The hook does ONLY: patch one column slot (or AbstractInstance handle via SetInstanceFromDataStatic/RemoveInstance, O(1) swap-patch) + insert/erase the stable handle in the grid cells it covers + insert/erase in the Z-band index + OR the touched tile id(s) into a monotonic DirtyTiles bitset. On the server it ALSO marks those tiles' content-hash version stale. No O(N) work, no coroutine cancel, no canvas touch. (Replaces today's O(N) redirector reindex + O(N) equal-Z scan + Cancel()+restart.)

(2) SERVER COMPUTE/STORE (server only, off the hot path): once per quiescence/net-tick, a UE::Tasks worker recomputes the content hash + packs the slim blob for each stale tile from the engine arrays (snapshotted on the game thread first). The new immutable TSharedRef snapshot atomically replaces the old (game-thread pointer swap); the version table updates. This is the single authoritative derive — shared across all joiners.

(3) STREAM TO CLIENTS (dedicated only): the server coalesces per-tile version bumps per net-tick and, per client, enqueues SendTaggedMessage for tiles in that client's AoI whose version the client lacks, ordered by distance from the client's map-viewport center (app-level AoI ordering, since the queue is FIFO). ReliableMessaging chunks/acks/windows the bytes over TCP/EOS/Steam. (On a listen host/single-player this entire step is stubbed — the client reads the host's indices directly.)

(4) CLIENT TILE CACHE (dedicated client): the RegisterTaggedMessageHandler callback receives a completed tile blob, validates the 1-byte protocol version + tile content version, idempotently clear-then-applies the slim records into its local AoI SoA store + grid, and marks the tile dirty for local render. Tiles outside AoI are evicted LRU.

(5) RENDER (client, or host in-process): the never-cancelled convergent compositor drains DirtyTiles under the frame-relative UE5Coro budget, prioritizing the current viewport. Per dirty tile it recomputes draw geometry via the shared ComputeDrawGeometry from the slim record + ClassDrawTable and emits it — Phase A: scissored HW clear + bounded FCanvas EndDraw per tile (separate GPU command buffer); Phase B: appends to the MakeCustomVerts per-instance buffer drawn by the Slate SLeafWidget in Z-band order; Phase C: patches the AbstractInstance custom data + triggers one debounced orthographic-tiled SceneCapture. The map UI (Slate/UMG) composites the result.

JOIN FLOW (fixes #9): client opens map -> sends initial viewport AoI -> server replies with the MANIFEST (tile ids + versions for that AoI) -> server streams the shared per-tile snapshots in AoI order via ReliableMessaging -> client renders progressively as tiles arrive. No global serialize, no per-joiner full copy (shared TSharedRef), no int16 counter, no unchecked Find(), no game-thread Archive<<CurrentBuildingData. Join memory O(joiners+AoI); join time = a few hundred bounded round-trips, not ~2000 RTTs + an O(N) synchronous serialize.

CHUNK-LOAD FLOW (O(1)): client enters a new WP-aligned region -> for each newly-relevant tile it checks its cached version against the server's last-known version (or requests the manifest delta) -> fetches only blobs it lacks. Never a recompute. Generation-guarded keys + PostLoadGame reconcile tolerate engine lightweight-index renumbering and streamed-out regions.

openQuestions: GetViewOwner/ShowOnlyActors capture isolation on the CSS 5.6.1 renderer fork is UNVERIFIED (the Cartograph_2.0 POC used exactly this and never compiled). Phase 4 must validate it on the fork before committing; if it fails, the gated GPU end-state is blocked and the Slate MakeCustomVerts path (Phase 3) becomes the permanent default.

AbstractInstance high-churn cost: Tessera's research cites UE5 ISM AddInstance/RemoveInstance regressions for high-churn megabases (Chaos collision rebuild). We disable collision and batch via MarkDirtyDeferred, but the render-state-dirty cost on rapid belt-drag at 1M buildings needs an empirical benchmark before Phase 4 is chosen over staying on Phase 3.

FInstanceOwnerHandlePtr is TSharedPtr<...,NotThreadSafe> (verified) = game-thread-only, so the worker-thread packing path (UE::Tasks) cannot touch handles. Confirm the volume of game-thread-only handle writes during a mass-paste stays within the frame budget, or fall back to a hand-rolled instance buffer only if it proves blocking.

Persistent-target preserve semantics on 5.6.1-CSS: verify the second BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget does NOT implicitly re-clear (the branch-history 'lines going crazy' note traces to exactly this) and that bAutoGenerateMips=false is honored, before relying on the Phase-2 persistent tile target.

WP cell granularity and whether a mod can observe cell load/unload events on the CSS fork is unverified - needed to hard-couple tile size to WP cells for O(1) chunk-load. The map-UI viewport AoI (what drives tile pulls) is explicitly NOT the world-streaming AoI; confirm the read-only WP source-position API is reachable from a GameFeature mod.

Lightweight-index renumbering: the engine can renumber AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem indices on its own removals. The generation-guarded {class,index} key + PostLoadGame reconcile must be validated against a real engine-side mass removal to ensure no handle aliasing.

ComputeDrawGeometry pixel-identity: the draw-time recompute must reproduce the old FillInCache math exactly or icons shift. Requires a diff-render harness over a large save during Phase 1 before the stored cache fields are deleted.

ReliableMessaging behavior under a multi-MB AoI burst on the live CSS dedicated-server net mode (TCP transport) is verified by source but not load-tested; confirm the windowed/acked path sustains a worst-case first-join AoI without head-of-line blocking given the strict-FIFO queue and by-value payload.

Single-precision FVector3f position (~0.05 cm error at the 7.5 km edge) forbids any exact-equality transform compare (the old value-quadtree identity). Audit for residual exact-equality position compares before switching identity to the handle.

Save persistence policy: confirm with the mod author whether to ship the optional IFGSaveInterface grid+slim-record cache at all, given the recomputable-cache stance - it trades save size for load time and adds version/reconcile surface; default OFF unless cold-load time is shown to be a problem.
